Bhola @ Shyam Bahadur vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12
March, 2024
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:48162
Court No. - 89
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 40956 of 2023
Applicant :- Bhola @ Shyam Bahadur 
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another 
Counsel for Applicant :- Araf Khan,Lihazur Rahman Khan Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Sadhna Rani (Thakur),J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for opposite parties and perused the record. 
By moving this application prayer is made to quash the cognizance order dated 25.09.2023 passed on the charge sheet dated 17.06.2023 and the entire criminal proceedings of Criminal Case No. 7356 of 2023, Crime No. 330 of 2022 under Section 3/7 Essential Commodities Act, Police Station Roravar, District Aligarh. 
As per the facts of the case, on 18.08.2022 an FIR was lodged by the Supply Officer, Piyush Kumar Gautam that on the basis of the information received, on 17.08.2022 when the disputed godown was inspected, five persons found there introduced themselves as the labourers and disclosed that they had been engaged there by Bhola s/o Ravneer Singh for loading the rice sacks in the truck. Later on,
on weighing the rice was found to be 154.15 qtls. Prima-facie, this rice appeared to be the rice, which is distributed at the fair price shops. Any document regarding the ownership of the rice could not be Bhola @ Shyam Bahadur vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149668726/
1 shown on the spot and prima facie it was found that the rice was sold/purchased illegally, which is the violation of the Government Order No. 3615/29-07-2003/M-11/94 dated 29.11.2003. The rice was seized and given into the custody of one Irshad, the fair price dealer with necessary instructions.
The memo was prepared as per law and after taking approval from the District Magistrate the FIR was lodged.
The only argument made by the learned counsel for the applicant is that for the offence under Section 7 of Essential Commodities Act, there must be violation of some control order, but in the FIR no control order has been mentioned rather a Government Order has been mentioned. In the absence of violation of any control order the prosecution against the applicant is impermissible. The applicant is the sole proprietor of M/s Bhola Trading Company registered under Rule 10(1) in Form GST REG-06. It works in the name and style as aforesaid and deals with transportation of edible s such as pulses, rice, chickpeas, pearl millet etc. The rice is generally purchased by the applicant from different wholesale godowns before its transportation to the retailer. The purchase bills dated 13.08.2022, 14.08.2022, 15.08.2022 and 17.08.2022 relating to purchase of the rice confiscated in the present case were placed before the court. After perusing these bills the rice has been released in favour of the applicant vide order dated 14.09.2022. 
The attention of the court is drawn towards some judgements of the Apex Court and this Court. If we go through the judgement in Prakash Babu Raghuvanshi Vs. State of M.P. (2004)7 Supreme Court Cases 490 and Nitin Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh, Misc. Criminal Case No. 24128 of 2018. It has been held therein that for prosecution under Section 7 of Essential Commodities Act there must be violation of some notified order/control order. In judgement Mohd. Kaleem Vs. State of U.P. & others, MANU/UP/2288/2019 , the coordinate bench of this court, though, found that provisions of some control order must have been violated for the application of Section 7 of Essential Commodities Act but as per facts of that case, the court found the petitioner having valid license of sales tax, valid license of Mandi Samiti for doing business of food stuff. The petitioner was also having IEC issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industries, Department of Commerce. In judgement Farmeeda Begum Vs. State of U.P. and others, MANU/UP/0879/2022 the coordinate bench of this court, though, opined the same view that some control order must be violated for the application of Section 7 of Essential Commodities Act but in para-9 of this judgement the court has quoted the view of the Apex Court in Prakash Babu Raghuvanshi Vs. State of M.P. (2004)7SCC 482 and observation in para-5 of this judgement has been cited as under:- 
"Section 7 refers to contravention of any order made under Section 3. It is essential for bringing in application of Section 7 to show that some order has been made under Section 3 and the order has been contravened. Section 3 deals with powers to control production, supply, distribution etc. of essential commodities. Exercise of such powers, can be done by "order". According to Section 2(c) "notified order" means an order notified in the official Gazettee, and Section (CC) provides that "order" includes a direction issued thereunder." 
In judgement Krishnapal Singh Kansana Vs. State of M.P. and another, MCRC 45489 of 2021, the coordinate bench of M.P. High Court found that prior permission of concerned Collector is much for Bhola @ Shyam Bahadur vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149668726/
2 filing FIR under the provisions of Essential Commodities Act. Further it was held that the control order must have been violated for lodging an FIR against him. 
Thus, the only argument of the learned counsel for the applicant on the basis of above judgements is again the same that for invoking the power to lodge an FIR under Section 3/7 of Essential Commodities Act there must be violation of some control order and in the FIR concerned the control order has not been mentioned, the violation of which can be claimed on the part of the applicant. 
Learned A.G.A., however, opposed the prayer and submitted that in the FIR the Government Order dated 29.07.2003 has been mentioned. He has drawn the attention of the court towards supplementary counter affidavit filed by him mentioning the Uttar Pradesh Essential Commodities (Regulation of Sale and Distribution Control) Order, 2016 and submitted that whereas the State Government is of the opinion that it is necessary and expedient so to do for maintaining the supply of foodgrains and other essential commodities and for securing their equitable distribution and availability on fair price under targeted public distribution system and with this aim the control order dated 29.06.2016 was passed. It is submitted that for the equitable distribution and availability of edibles on fair price, it is necessary that a person dealing in sale and purchase of foodgrains must have the necessary license and registration etc. But neither any license nor any registration has been shown by the applicant to deal with business of sale and purchase of foodgrains. 
A reply on behalf of District Supply Officer has been placed before the court, whereby it is said that at the time of inspection no stock or any other register, any bill regarding sale and purchase or regarding loading of rice, license of Mandi Samiti and any license issued by Food Safety and Medicine Cosmetics and the license issued by the Weight and Measurement department were placed before the team. None of these documents could be placed before the team the next day till the filing of FIR or till today. The applicant being a habitual culprit in blackmarketing and hoarding of foodgrains is not entitled for any relief from this court. However, it is submitted that against the applicant six more cases of the similar nature from the year 2019 till 2022 registered in different police stations of Aligarh are pending. The description of these six cases has been given in the comments by the District Supply Officer. 
From perusal of the record, it is found that the applicant was not found on the spot at the time of inspection. Five labourers were found on the spot, who disclosed the name of the applicant as the person who had employed the labourers for loading 154.15 qtls. of rice on the truck. In his written submission learned counsel for the applicant has mentioned that the applicant being the sole proprietor of M/s Bhola Trading Company works in the name and style as above and deals with the transportation of edibles like pulses, rice and pearly millet etc. The company is registered under Section 10(1) in the Form GST Reg 06. The rice is generally purchased by the applicant from different wholesale godowns before its transportation to the retailer. This is admission on the part of the applicant that he is not merely a transporter of the foodgrains rather he is involved in the business of sale and purchase of different foodgrains and for this business he is not having any license of sales tax, license of Mandi Samiti or having IEC issued by Ministry of Commerce and Bhola @ Shyam Bahadur vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149668726/
3 Industries, Department of Commerce. 
If we come to the main argument raised by the learned counsel for the applicant that in the FIR no control order has been mentioned, the violation of which is said to be done by the applicant and without violation of any control order the applicant cannot be held liable for punishment under Section 7 of Essential Commodities Act, admittedly, any order passed in compliance of Section 3 of Essential Commodities Act, 1955 must be violated for application of punishment under Section 7 of Essential Commodities Act. Sub-section (1) of Section 3 of Essential Commodities Act runs as under:-
3. Powers to control production, supply, distribution etc., of essential commodities.--
( 1) If the Central Government is of opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do for maintaining or increasing supplies of any essential commodity or for securing their equitable distribution and availability at fair prices, [or for securing any essential commodity for the defence of India or the efficient conduct of military operation], it may, by order, provide for regulating or prohibiting the production,
supply and distribution thereof and trade and commerce therein. 
Thus, the Central Government may pass any order regulating or prohibiting the production, supply and distribution of any essential commodity and trade and commerce therein, which shows that there must have been an order passed by the Government. If we go through the definition of the word 'order', which is defined in Section 2(CC) 'order' includes a direction issued thereunder. If the definition of the word 'notified order' as defined in Section 2(c) is seen, 'notified order' means an order notified in the official gazette. Certainly the Government Order mentioned in the FIR is an order which is notified in the official gazettee. This Government Order has been placed by the learned counsel for the applicant, which is apended at page 5 of the supplementary affidavit filed by the learned counsel for the applicant on 28.11.2023. By this Government Order the Government Order dated 09.12.2000 and Government Order dated 30.10.2001 were amended to the extent that these two Government Orders would not apply to the persons involved in blackmarketing, hoarding,
adulterating the foodgrains. The Government Orders dated 19.12.2000 and 30.10.2001 have also been placed before the court vide second supplementary affidavit dated 14.02.2024 by the learned counsel for the applicant. By the Government Order dated 19.12.2000 it was decided that no case would be registered against a businessmen under Essential Commodities Act. Vide Government Order dated 30.10.2001 the cases under Essential Commodities Act registered against the businessmen were ordered to be withdrawn in public interest. Thus, it is claimed that no control order has been violated as per the Government Order mentioned in the FIR, so the relief is claimed accordingly. 
It is clear from the definition of the order as mentioned in Section 2(c) and (CC) of the Act that the order included a direction issued therein and the notified order means an order notified in the official gazettee. Certainly, the Government Order mentioned in the FIR is a notified order which is notified in the official gazettee. Regarding the question what order has been violated by the applicant, it is clear that for maintaining the supply of foodgrains and other essential commodities and for securing their equitable distribution and availability at fair price under targeted public Bhola @ Shyam Bahadur vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149668726/
4 distribution system the Government had power to pass orders and by mentioning Government Order dated 29.11.2003 in the FIR it is clear that the exemption of filing cases against the petty businessmen or the order of withdrawing such cases against the petty businessmen under the provisions of Essential Commodities Act has been withdrawn by this order. The businessmen involved in blackmarketing, hoarding and adulteration of foodgrains are kept away from exemption of filing cases against them. It means that the provisions of Essential Commodities Act would apply to the businessmen indulged in blackmarketing, hoarding or adulteration of various foodgrains and the applicant having no license of sales tax, Mandi Samiti or not having IEC issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industries, Department of Commerce, prima-facie, can be said to be violating the Government Order dated 29.11.2003 mentioned in the FIR. Admittedly, before filing of FIR an approval of District Magistrate was taken by the officer concerned. 
In the opinion of the court, the applicant who could not show any license or document regarding business of sale and purchase of rice cannot take benefit of his argument at this stage that neither any control order has been mentioned in the FIR nor any violation of any control order has been made by him. The arguments of learned counsel for the applicant do not inspire confidence of the court. The arguments having no merit, the applicant is not entitled for the relief claimed. 
The application is hereby dismissed. 
Order Date :- 12.3.2024 Gss/gp  Bhola @ Shyam Bahadur vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149668726/

the coordinate bench of M.P. High Court found that prior permission of concerned Collector is much for Bhola @ Shyam Bahadur vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149668726/
2 filing FIR under the provisions of Essential Commodities Act.
The applicant being a habitual culprit in blackmarketing and hoarding of foodgrains is not entitled for any relief from this court.
This is admission on the part of the applicant that he is not merely a transporter of the foodgrains rather he is involved in the business of sale and purchase of different foodgrains and for this business he is not having any license of sales tax, license of Mandi Samiti or having IEC issued by Ministry of Commerce and Bhola @ Shyam Bahadur vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149668726/
3 Industries, Department of Commerce.
By the Government Order dated 19.12.2000 it was decided that no case would be registered against a businessmen under Essential Commodities Act.

It is clear from the definition of the order as mentioned in Section 2(c) and (CC) of the Act that the order included a direction issued therein and the notified order means an order notified in the official gazettee.
Certainly, the Government Order mentioned in the FIR is a notified order which is notified in the official gazettee.
The businessmen involved in blackmarketing, hoarding and adulteration of foodgrains are kept away from exemption of filing cases against them.
It means that the provisions of Essential Commodities Act would apply to the businessmen indulged in blackmarketing, hoarding or adulteration of various foodgrains and the applicant having no license of sales tax, Mandi Samiti or not having IEC issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industries, Department of Commerce, prima-facie, can be said to be violating the Government Order dated 29.11.2003 mentioned in the FIR.
Admittedly, before filing of FIR an approval of District Magistrate was taken by the officer concerned.
In the opinion of the court, the applicant who could not show any license or document regarding business of sale and purchase of rice cannot take benefit of his argument at this stage that neither any control order has been mentioned in the FIR nor any violation of any control order has been made by him.
